body.statement: If \(B\ge2\) and \(\varepsilon\le\min\{p,1-p\}\), then, with \(r=1\), the laws \(P^{\Delta}\) and \(P^+\) satisfy the iid-innovation, graph-equivariance, graph-edge-range, score-locality, outcome-envelope, wavewise-Bernoulli, cross-wave-independence, and exposure-positivity conditions listed in \(\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\).  Under \(P^{\Delta}\), \(h_i=U_i-U_{i-1}\) and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\); under \(P^+\), \(h_i=U_i\) and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=1\).
body.justification: The paired laws verify that the null contains heterogeneous effects and that the alternative class is nonempty under one common envelope.
body.gap: LiWager2022 discusses assignment-dominated limits in a dense graphon setting; these radius-one line examples isolate cancellation and positive Palm variation in the exact class used by the diagnostic.
body.consumer: The two laws provide finite-range simulation benchmarks for checking rejection frequencies and power calculations.
body.proof_tex:
Set \(r=1\).  Under each law in \(\operatorname{def:boundary-witnesses}\), the variables \((U_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}\) are independent Rademacher variables, so in particular
\[
 \mathbb E_P[U_i]=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P[U_iU_j]=\mathbf 1\{i=j\}.
\]
The deterministic nearest-neighbor line is translation equivariant and every neighbor of \(i\) lies in \(\{i-1,i,i+1\}\), proving the graph-equivariance and graph-edge-range conditions.  For every fixed assignment \(d\), the pair consisting of exposure and outcome is measurable with respect to
\[
 \sigma(U_j,d_j:i-1\le j\le i+1),
\]
because the first schedule uses only \((U_{i-1},U_i,d_i)\), while the second uses only \((U_i,d_i)\).  Since \(|U_i|=1\) almost surely and \(d_i\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 |(U_i-U_{i-1})d_i|
 \le |U_i|+|U_{i-1}|=2\le B,
 \qquad
 |U_id_i|\le1\le B.
\]
Thus the support and locality requirements hold under the stated condition \(B\ge2\).

By the assignment part of \(\operatorname{def:boundary-witnesses}\), conditional on \(\mathcal F_U\), the coordinates within each wave are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) variables and the two waves are conditionally independent.  Because \(E_i(D^{(w)},G)=D_i^{(w)}\), the two relevant conditional exposure probabilities are
\[
 \pi_i(e_1)=P(D_i^{(w)}=1\mid\mathcal F_U)=p,
 \qquad
 \pi_i(e_0)=P(D_i^{(w)}=0\mid\mathcal F_U)=1-p.
\]
The primitive restriction \(p\in(0,1)\) makes both denominators positive, and the displayed hypothesis \(\varepsilon\le\min\{p,1-p\}\) proves exposure positivity.  This establishes every primitive listed in the narrowed statement.

For the remaining calculations, define the \(\mathcal F_U\)-measurable coefficients
\[
 A_i^{\Delta}=U_i-U_{i-1},
 \qquad
 A_i^+=U_i.
\]
Under the corresponding law the realized outcome is \(A_iD_i^{(w)}\).  Since \(e_1=1\), \(e_0=0\), \(D_i^{(w)}(1-D_i^{(w)})=0\), and \((D_i^{(w)})^2=D_i^{(w)}\), direct substitution into the defining exposure-IPW formula gives, for either coefficient \(A_i\in\{A_i^{\Delta},A_i^+\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Z_i^{(w)}
 &=A_iD_i^{(w)}
   \left\{\frac{D_i^{(w)}}p-
   \frac{1-D_i^{(w)}}{1-p}\right\}\\
 &=A_i\frac{D_i^{(w)}}p.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This variable is bounded because \(|A_i|\le2\) and \(p>0\), so its conditional expectation exists.  Using the \(\mathcal F_U\)-measurability of \(A_i\) and \(\mathbb E_P[D_i^{(w)}\mid\mathcal F_U]=p\),
\[
 m_i
 =\mathbb E_P[Z_i^{(w)}\mid\mathcal F_U]
 =\frac{A_i}{p}\mathbb E_P[D_i^{(w)}\mid\mathcal F_U]
 =A_i.
\]

Under \(P^{\Delta}\), the Rademacher means yield
\[
 \tau_{\mathrm P}=\mathbb E_{P^{\Delta}}[m_0]
 =\mathbb E[U_0-U_{-1}]=0,
 \qquad
 h_i=m_i-\tau_{\mathrm P}=U_i-U_{i-1}.
\]
For every integer \(k\), expansion followed by the Rademacher covariance identity above gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \gamma_h(k)
 &=\mathbb E[(U_0-U_{-1})(U_k-U_{k-1})]\\
 &=2\mathbf 1\{k=0\}
   -\mathbf 1\{k=1\}
   -\mathbf 1\{k=-1\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
In particular, because \(r=1\) makes the defining covariance window \(\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}\),
\[
 \Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}
 =\sum_{k=-2}^{2}\gamma_h(k)
 =2-1-1=0.
\]

Under \(P^+\), the same conditional-expectation calculation instead gives
\[
 \tau_{\mathrm P}=\mathbb E_{P^+}[U_0]=0,
 \qquad
 h_i=U_i.
\]
Independence and the Rademacher second moment imply
\[
 \gamma_h(k)=\mathbb E[U_0U_k]=\mathbf 1\{k=0\},
\]
and therefore
\[
 \Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}
 =\sum_{k=-2}^{2}\gamma_h(k)=1.
\]
These are exactly the two asserted population-variance values.
